title: SessionStart hook output exceeds Claude Code's inline limit: the seat section is cut off
description: A seat on another project woke with crew-wake and ran a whole session without its seat identity. The SessionStart hook printed 24.5KB / 204 lines; Claude Code did not inline it but wrote 'Output too large (24KB). Full output saved to: <session dir>/tool-results/hook-....txt' with a 2KB preview that ended inside PRIME.md's Commands section. The seat section (# You are <seat>, SEAT.md, last diary entry, beads in progress, inbox) started at byte 20,756 and was never read. Layout of the output: PRIME.md 3.2KB, then '## Persistent Memories (29)' 17.6KB (72%, printed by bd prime, grows with every bd remember), then the seat section 3.8KB. CLAUDE.md's health check ('context did not start with # Beads workflow') passed because the first 2KB was exactly that. User's brief: investigate and present options with trade-offs, do not implement yet. Preference stated: PRIME.md and the seat section first, memories last, so a truncation only ever costs memories. Things to check: whether bd prime can print the rules without the memories; whether memories should be capped in the hook (bytes, count, keys only); the seat line as the very first line as cheap insurance; whether hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext has the same size limit as plain stdout; the actual inline threshold on this Claude Code version and whether it is documented; PRIME.md's 'append your diary entry if you have a seat' reads as optional, and the CLAUDE.md health check should look for the seat line.
design: Shipped as 1.3.0. SessionStart: the seat line is the first line of output, then 'if this output was saved to a file, read it', then bd prime --no-memories (falls back to bd prime on an older bd), the seat section, and a topic index of memory keys instead of their text; the whole output is built in a function and measured, and cut at 9,500 bytes with a note if a seat's files ever push it over, so the seat can never be lost to the 10,000-character cap. Memories: a new UserPromptSubmit hook (prompt-submit.sh -> memories.py match) dumps bd memories --json once per prompt, matches the prompt's words of four or more characters minus stopwords against key and value, ranks by distinct matches, injects the top 5 under 4,000 characters as additionalContext, and injects each key once per context (a seen-file per session id in TMPDIR, cleared by the SessionStart hook, which fires on every new context). PRIME.md states the key convention <topic>-<slug> and that memories arrive with the prompt. Rejected: capping bd prime's memories (alphabetical survivors, finding 10); keys only in the hook (an index of topics is smaller and scales further); separate SessionStart hook commands per part (order in context not guaranteed, memories still over the cap); embedding search (bd has none, keyword match is the lazy version with a known ceiling).
close_reason: Released as 1.3.0 (tag crew--v1.3.0). Shipped: seat line first in the SessionStart output plus a read-the-saved-file line, bd prime --no-memories with a fallback, a topic index of memories instead of their text, the whole output measured and cut at 9,500 bytes; a UserPromptSubmit hook (prompt-submit.sh, memories.py) that injects the memories matching the prompt via SQLite FTS5 with Porter stems and BM25, five at most, 4,000 characters, each once per context, weak matches dropped at 40% of the best score; PRIME.md's key convention and seat check; the health-check wording in the adopt template and this repo's instructions. Verified: strict gate; direct hook runs for seat, no seat, new seat; the prompt hook's seen-file round trip; matches on a project with 30 memories; an end-to-end claude -p session with --plugin-dir in which the model quoted the seat line and the injected memory's key. Left out: semantic search (embeddings), recorded as the upgrade path in the bead and README.

comments.author: siler
comments.text: Findings (Claude Code 2.1.301, bd 1.3.0). (1) The inline limit is 10,000 characters per hook string, preview 2,000 chars; found in the binary (persist function: threshold 1e4, preview 2000) and documented at code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks: 'A hook's additionalContext, systemMessage, and initialUserMessage strings, and its plain stdout, are capped at 10,000 characters ... this cap has no setting or environment variable to raise it ... Claude can read the file, but Claude Code doesn't ask it to.' (2) hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext goes through the same function with the same default threshold, measured per field. Live test: a 24KB hook in both forms, model asked for the first and last marker line: first seen, last not seen, both forms. (3) bd prime has --no-memories, --memories-only, --max-memories N, --max-memory-chars N (entries only, header and banner excluded) and --hook-json; its help says 'hosts truncate silently'. Caps are ALPHABETICAL, not newest first, with a banner 'N more memories are not shown ... bd memories <keyword>'. bd memories --json is key->content, no dates, so newest-first is not available from the CLI. (4) bd's default template starts with a banner '[bd prime] If this output is truncated by your host, read the full persisted hook output before continuing'; a custom .beads/PRIME.md (ours) replaces that banner, so the kit removed bd's own safeguard. (5) Sizes: PRIME.md 3,159 B; seat section 2.1 KB (kit seats) to 3.8 KB (the affected seat); memories average ~600 B each, 30 entries = 18 KB; keys-only listing of 31 memories = 1.3 KB. Budget under 10,000 with order PRIME+seat+memories: about 3-4.5 KB for memories, i.e. 5-7 entries.

comments.author: siler
comments.text: More findings. (6) Boundary confirmed live: a 9,977-byte plain-stdout hook was inlined whole (both markers seen); 10,489 bytes was persisted (last marker not seen). (7) Over the cap the output is not cut at 10,000: the WHOLE string is replaced by the path plus the first 2,000 chars. PRIME.md alone is 3,159 bytes, so reordering to PRIME, seat, memories does NOT save the seat on its own: a 24 KB output would still show only the first 2 KB of PRIME.md. The seat survives only if the total stays under 10,000, or if the seat line sits inside the first 2,000 chars. (8) The inlined note reads 'Output too large (25.1KB). Full output saved to: <path>' then 'Preview (first 2KB):' and does not ask the model to read the file. (9) The hook result is prefixed 'SessionStart:startup hook success:' in context, and other plugins' SessionStart hooks can precede ours, so a 'context starts with' health check is already not literal. (10) Memory dates are not reachable: bd memories --json is key->content and bd sql is 'not yet supported in embedded mode', so newest-first needs an upstream bd change.

comments.author: siler
comments.text: Options presented to the user (not implemented): A. Reorder in session-start.sh: bd prime --no-memories, seat section, then bd prime --memories-only; two bd calls. On its own it does not save the seat (finding 7). B. Keep the total under 10,000: measure what the script has printed so far and give the rest to bd prime --memories-only --max-memory-chars <remaining>; bd prints the elision banner. Alphabetical survivors, 5-7 entries at today's sizes. C. Seat line as the first line of output, plus a one-line 'if this output was saved to a file, read it before anything else' (bd's own banner, which our custom PRIME.md dropped). Insurance inside the 2,000-char preview. D. Keys-only memory listing (1.3 KB for 31 keys) with 'bd memories <key>' to read one; scales to hundreds, costs the always-present promise. E. Split into separate SessionStart hook commands (rules / seat / memories), each measured on its own; buys decoupling but memories over 10K are still persisted, and multi-hook order in context is not guaranteed. F. Wording: PRIME.md 'append your diary entry if you have a seat' -> check echo $SEAT and if set but no '# You are' section in context, the wake-up output was cut; health check in CLAUDE.md/adopt to look for the seat line. Newest-first is not possible from bd's CLI today (finding 10).

comments.author: siler
comments.text: User asked whether alphabetical order is odd. Checked every place bd exposes memories: bd memories --json (key->value), bd recall --json (found/key/schema_version/value), bd export --include-memories ({_type:memory,key,value}). None carries a timestamp, so bd stores no date for memories and no client can order them by age. Alphabetical is the only order bd has. Side finding: bd export excludes memories by default, so .beads/issues.jsonl carries none and the kit's SessionEnd hook and handoff export leave them machine-local; filed as a follow-up.

comments.author: siler
comments.text: User: 'We need a system that scales with many, many memories.' Proposed design (not implemented): wake-up carries an index, content arrives when relevant. (1) SessionStart: seat first, total guarded under 10,000, bd prime --no-memories, then a topic index of memory keys (distinct first word of the key with counts, a few hundred bytes at any count) and 'bd memories <word> reads them'. (2) UserPromptSubmit hook: one bd memories --json dump (0.2 s measured at 30 entries, search is case-insensitive substring over key and value), match the prompt's distinctive words against key and value in-process, rank by matches, inject the top few as additionalContext under a ~4 KB cap. Scales to thousands with one bd call per prompt. (3) Hygiene: PRIME.md states keys as <topic>-<slug> so the index and manual search stay meaningful; ck-eoq makes the store travel with the repo. Replaces bd's own memory section (always --no-memories). Trade-offs: keyword matching, not semantic; ~0.3 s per prompt; relevance decided by the hook, misses cost one manual search. Alternative trigger considered: PreToolUse on Edit/Write/Read injecting memories that name the touched path; more precise for code gotchas, fires often, kept as a later addition.

comments.author: siler
comments.text: Built and verified, not committed (awaiting the user's word on the release). Checks: sh -n on all hooks and ast.parse on memories.py pass; claude plugin validate passes without --strict (the --strict failure is a pre-existing warning about CLAUDE.md at the plugin root, filed separately). Direct runs: as a seat the wake-up is 5,944 bytes with the seat line first, PRIME.md, the seat section and the memory index; 'no seat' and 'new seat' print their heading first. Prompt hook: a prompt about the hook output cap injects that memory (834 chars, 0.21 s); the same prompt again injects nothing (seen-file); the SessionStart hook removes the seen-file; an unrelated prompt and a non-crew project print nothing. On a project with 30 memories: index 0.27 s, 'run the playwright QA in headless chromium against the dev server' returns the four headless-playwright memories plus the dev-server one (0.28 s); 'fix the django migration that keeps being regenerated' first missed the regenerating-migration memory (no stem, alphabetical tie-break), fixed with a 4-suffix stem and a key bonus, now it is second of five. End to end with claude -p --plugin-dir on this repo as siler: the model quoted the seat line as the first line of the hook output and the matched memory's key from the UserPromptSubmit context. The kit's two memories were renamed to hooks-* per the new convention.

comments.author: siler
comments.text: User: 'let's do FTS5 first'. memories.py match now loads the unseen memories into an in-memory SQLite FTS5 table (tokenize=porter), queries the prompt's words OR-ed, orders by bm25(m, 3.0, 1.0) (key weighted 3x), takes TOP 5, and drops matches whose score is weaker than 40% of the best (bm25 is negative). Stopwords extended with prompt verbs (fix, add, run, update, discussed...). Measured on the 30-memory project: 'fix the django migration that keeps being regenerated' now returns regenerating-migration, keepdb-stale-migration, makemigrations-check and nothing else (1,560 chars; before FTS5 the first was missed, before the cutoff two unrelated ones padded the list); 'why does curl ... stale Content-Length' returns only dev-server-curl-needs-gzip (634 chars, was 2,668); 'please fix the thing we discussed' returns nothing (was one unrelated memory); 'gzip?' alone finds its memory; FTS5 keywords (NOT, AND) and quotes in a prompt are quoted into the query and do not break it. 0.26-0.30 s per prompt, unchanged. sqlite 3.45.1 here; FTS5 has shipped in SQLite since 3.9 (2015).

title: crew-wake new: the new seat does not start setting itself up
description: User: "This session has been created with the crew awake, but no hook has started to finish setting up the new seat. That's a bug as well. Address it." crew-wake new opened the session, the SessionStart hook printed '## New seat', and then the session sat idle until the user typed a prompt.
design: Root cause: SessionStart hook stdout is context only; a hook cannot start a turn, so the 'Before any other work' instruction waits for the user's first message. Fix in bin/crew-wake: when crew/<seat>/SEAT.md is missing (the same test the hook uses), pass claude an initial prompt, so the session starts the setup itself. Rejected: making the hook louder (still no turn); a seat-name check for 'new' (the hook keys on SEAT.md, keep one test). The prompt goes before "$@" so optional-valued flags like --resume cannot swallow it.
close_reason: bin/crew-wake now passes an initial prompt when crew/<seat>/SEAT.md is missing, placed before the extra args. README 'Adding a seat' step 1 and CHANGELOG 1.1.1 say so; plugin.json at 1.1.1. Verified with a stub claude on PATH: 'crew-wake new --resume' passes the prompt ahead of --resume, 'crew-wake siler --plugin-dir x' passes none. Quality gate passed (plugin validate --strict, sh -n on hooks and crew-wake). Not verified: a real interactive 'crew-wake new' launch. Not done: commit, claude plugin tag, push (the user did not ask).

comments.author: siler
comments.text: Released after close: the user asked for it. Commits 89c241f (seat) and 21af64b (fix, 1.1.1), tag crew--v1.1.1 (claude plugin tag .), pushed with --follow-tags; origin has main at 21af64b and the tag.

title: SessionEnd auto-commit of the beads export and the seat's diary, opt-in per project
description: User: 'can we add a configurable option to auto-commit the diary and export created in the SessionEnd hook?' Today the SessionEnd hook only writes .beads/issues.jsonl; the diary and export sit uncommitted until someone commits them (walter's handoff sat in the tree for two weeks). Wanted: a switch that makes the hook commit them.
design: Opt-in by a file, crew/autocommit, the kit's existing pattern for per-project settings (crew/prefix); absent means today's behaviour, since PRIME.md says not to commit unless asked. The SessionEnd command moves from an inline string in hooks.json to hooks/session-end.sh so it is readable and sh -n checked. It commits only .beads/issues.jsonl and crew/$SEAT/ (the diary, and a new seat's card), with a pathspec commit (git commit -- paths) so other staged changes stay staged and uncommitted; a merge or rebase in progress makes the partial commit fail, and the hook stays silent. Message 'chore: <seat>'s handoff' or 'chore: beads export' without a seat. No push: that is a separate decision and can become a second value of the file later. Rejected: a bd config key (ties a crew policy to bd's config), an environment variable (per machine, but the handoff policy is the project's), committing the whole tree (would sweep up code the user has not reviewed).
close_reason: Released as 1.3.0 (tag crew--v1.3.0). hooks/session-end.sh: export with memories, and with crew/autocommit present a pathspec commit of .beads/issues.jsonl and crew/$SEAT/ as 'chore: <seat>'s handoff' (or 'chore: beads export' without a seat); no push. Verified in a scratch repo (off, on with an unrelated staged file left staged, nothing changed, no seat, no git). Documented in README (Files, Ending a session, The kit), the adopt skill asks about it. Side fix: export.auto off here and in the adopt skill, since bd's auto-export cannot write memories.

comments.author: siler
comments.text: Scratch-repo test of hooks/session-end.sh, five cases: without crew/autocommit the export is written and nothing is committed; with it and an unrelated staged change, the commit 'chore: zed's handoff' holds exactly .beads/issues.jsonl and crew/zed/diary.md while app.txt stays staged; a second run with nothing changed adds no commit; without a seat a changed bead gives 'chore: beads export' with the export only; outside a git repo the hook is silent. Side finding while building: bd's auto-export (export.auto true, set by the adopt skill) refuses to overwrite an issues.jsonl that holds memory records ('auto-export shrink guard') and prints a warning on every bd write, and bd has no config key to include memories in auto-export (export.auto, path, interval, git-add only). The kit never relied on it (the handoff skill calls it unreliable; the SessionEnd hook and handoff export explicitly), so export.auto is now off here and the adopt skill no longer turns it on.

title: Memories are not in .beads/issues.jsonl: bd export excludes them unless --include-memories
description: Found while investigating ck-6l5: bd export (the SessionEnd hook and the handoff skill both run it without flags) leaves out memories by default 'because they may contain sensitive agent context'. So bd remember entries never reach git and a second machine, or a fresh clone, starts with none, while PRIME.md tells seats to put project knowledge there. Decide: export with --include-memories (memories are project knowledge in a repo that is already the record), or tell seats memories are local. Note the kit repo is public, so the crewkit memories themselves must stay free of other projects' names.
close_reason: User: yes, memories go in the committed record. Added --include-memories to the SessionEnd export in hooks/hooks.json, the handoff skill's export step, and the adopt skill's two export mentions; PRIME.md's Git section, README's Memories section and the 1.3.0 changelog say so. Ran the export: .beads/issues.jsonl now carries 12 issues and the kit's 2 memories as _type:memory records. Round trip through bd import verified earlier in scratch repos. Strict gate passes. Ships with 1.3.0, not committed yet.

comments.author: siler
comments.text: Round trip verified in two scratch beads repos: bd export --include-memories writes {_type:memory,key,value} records next to the issues (1 issue + 1 memory exported), and bd import on the other side restores them ('Imported 1 issues and 1 memories'; bd memories lists it). bd import's help says memory records are detected automatically, so the kit's existing import at SessionStart needs no change. The fix is one flag in three places: the SessionEnd command in hooks/hooks.json, step 3 of skills/handoff/SKILL.md, step 7 of skills/adopt/SKILL.md. Cost: memories become part of the committed record, public in a public repo; bd excludes them by default for that reason. Not applied, awaiting the user's decision.

comments.author: siler
comments.text: Follow-up: with memories in issues.jsonl, bd's auto-export refuses to overwrite the file (shrink guard) and warns on every write. export.auto is now false in this repo and the adopt skill no longer sets it; the changelog tells existing projects to turn it off. The explicit exports (SessionEnd hook, handoff) are the record.

title: Configurable seat-name theme: crew/THEME.md, Stargate by default
description: User: 'I would like you to implement a configurable theme. By default, it should also be Stargate as it is now, but inside of the crew folder of each repository, the repository can have a THEME.md that can be altered. When you are initialising a repository and setting it up new, there should be a THEME.md created with the current description of the stargate theme that the user can then edit before they add a seat.'
design: The default theme is one file at the kit root, THEME.md (canon, pool, citation shape), next to PRIME.md. /crew:adopt copies it to crew/THEME.md once; after that it is the project's and the kit never overwrites it (unlike PRIME.md). The SessionStart hook's New seat note names the theme file to use: crew/THEME.md if present, else the kit's THEME.md, so projects adopted before this release keep Stargate with no change. README 'Adding a seat' keeps the generic rules (unique in project, lowercase ASCII dir, roster check) and points at the theme instead of listing Stargate names. Rejected: a theme setting in crew/prefix-style one-liners or several bundled themes to choose from - the user asked for one editable description, and a free-text file is what a seat reads anyway. Rejected: copying THEME.md into the kit's own crew/ - the fallback covers already-adopted projects, this one included.
close_reason: Shipped as 1.2.0 (not yet committed or tagged): new kit-root THEME.md (Stargate canon, pool, citation shape); /crew:adopt copies it to crew/THEME.md and the roster template points at it; the New seat hook note names crew/THEME.md, or the kit's THEME.md when the project has none; README (Files, Adding a seat, The kit, Adopt) and CHANGELOG updated. Verified: hook run in a scratch bd project without and with crew/THEME.md prints the kit path and crew/THEME.md respectively; quality gate passed (plugin validate --strict, sh -n on hooks and crew-wake). Not done: a live /crew:adopt run; the kit's own crew/ has no THEME.md and falls back to the default.

title: Handoff skill: a seat declared this session still has SEAT=new
description: A seat that declares itself in a 'crew-wake new' session keeps SEAT=new (and BEADS_ACTOR=new) until relaunched. The handoff skill says to append to crew/$SEAT/diary.md, which would be crew/new/diary.md, a folder that does not exist. Siler hit this at its first handoff and wrote to crew/siler/diary.md by hand. The skill should say: if you declared a seat this session, use its name.
design: Two sentences, no code: the handoff skill's preamble says a seat declared this session uses its declared name wherever $SEAT appears and adds --actor <name> to bd writes; README 'Adding a seat' step 3 says the same at declaration time, since the first beads (ck-itg) are written before the relaunch. Rejected: making crew-wake or the hook rewrite SEAT after declaration (a running session cannot change its own env; the hook only adds context). Verified bd --actor on a create in a scratch beads repo: 'Created by: probe-name'. Released as 1.2.1 (patch: wording).
close_reason: Shipped in 1.2.1 (commit c069a38, tag crew--v1.2.1, pushed): handoff skill preamble and README 'Adding a seat' step 3 say a seat declared this session uses its declared name for crew/<name>/ and --actor <name> on bd writes until the relaunch. Verified: bd --actor on a create in a scratch beads repo gives 'Created by: <name>'; quality gate passed (plugin validate --strict, sh -n on the three scripts). Not verified live: the next crew-wake new seat's first handoff is the real test. Left out: making crew-wake or the hook fix SEAT after declaration; a running session cannot change its own env.

title: Set up beads and crew seats for the kit's own development
description: The user, 2026-09-29, while building the kit: 'there definitely needs to be a Bead: <id> in the commit IDs ... any further enhancements will be done in the crewkit repo, which will have its own beads setup as any other project does.' Then: 'set up and add it as a second commit'. So this repo adopts its own kit: beads (prefix ck), crew/ for seats, CLAUDE.md with the beads rules and this repo's own rules, landed as the commit after 1.1.0.
design: Followed the /crew:adopt steps. Undid the commit bd init makes on its own so the setup lands as one commit with a Bead trailer. No crew/prefix: the folder name crewkit is already short. No TODO.md or AGENTS.md to convert. The quality gate in CLAUDE.md is plugin validation plus a shell syntax check, since the kit has no test suite.
close_reason: This repo now runs on its own kit: beads (prefix ck, export.auto on), crew/ (pointer README, empty roster, Stargate canon), CLAUDE.md with this repo's rules (public: no other project's names or ids, no emails, no Claude-Session links; Bead trailers; releases per README; quality gate) and the beads section. bd init's own commit was undone so the setup lands as the second commit, after 1.1.0. Verified: the installed kit's SessionStart hook in this folder prints the beads workflow and '## No seat' and copied PRIME.md into .beads/; the quality gate passes (strict plugin validation, sh -n on all three scripts); a grep of the new files finds no other project's names, emails or session links. Not done: the first seat (the user runs crew-wake new here). No plugin release: nothing the plugin ships changed.

title: Quality gate fails on Claude Code 2.1.301: 'claude plugin validate --strict' warns about CLAUDE.md at the plugin root
description: Found while verifying ck-6l5: claude plugin validate --strict . fails on HEAD too (checked in a clean worktree), with 'CLAUDE.md at the plugin root is not loaded as project context. To ship context with your plugin, use a skill instead.' The CLAUDE.md is this repo's working instructions, not plugin context, so the warning is noise for us, but --strict turns it into a failure. Options: drop --strict from the gate in CLAUDE.md, or move the repo instructions somewhere the validator ignores. The non-strict validate passes.
close_reason: Moved CLAUDE.md to .claude/CLAUDE.md with git mv (the user chose this over dropping --strict). claude plugin validate --strict . now passes, sh -n on all hooks and ast.parse on memories.py pass; a .claude/CLAUDE.md was shown to load as project instructions in a throwaway project before the move. CHANGELOG notes the move under 1.3.0. Not committed.

comments.author: siler
comments.text: Details. The warning: 'root: CLAUDE.md at the plugin root is not loaded as project context. To ship context with your plugin, use a skill (skills/<name>/SKILL.md) instead.' The validator assumes a CLAUDE.md inside a plugin is meant for the projects that install the plugin, and warns that it will not reach them. Ours is the opposite: instructions for working on this repo, which Claude Code loads from the checkout as usual. So the warning is noise for us, but --strict ('treat warnings as errors ... use in CI') makes the gate fail. Not new: every Claude Code version on this machine (2.1.289 of Oct 5 through 2.1.301) fails strict on HEAD; no older binary is here to find when it started. The plugin validate command has no ignore option (only --json and --strict). Verified fix: move the file to .claude/CLAUDE.md. In a worktree of HEAD with that move, claude plugin validate --strict passes; and a throwaway project with only .claude/CLAUDE.md had its content loaded as project instructions (claude -p answered with the codeword from it). value: A SessionStart hook only adds context; it cannot start a turn. Anything a seat must do at wake-up without the user typing needs crew-wake's initial prompt (see ck-hmi).

Claude Code inlines a hook's output only up to 10,000 characters per string (plain stdout, and each of additionalContext / systemMessage / initialUserMessage separately); over that it saves the text to <session dir>/tool-results/hook-*.txt and inlines a 2,000-char preview with the path, without telling the model to read it. Not configurable (checked 2.1.301 and the hooks docs). Every byte the SessionStart hook prints must fit under that; the seat line goes first (see ck-6l5).
